analysis: Both changed files are test-only; no production source, protocol, key custody, attestation or authorization paths change. (1) StandaloneServerModelAdmissionTests.swift head lines 517-536 add headroomGateReleasesRetainedKVSegmentsBeforeRefusing. It uses test hooks and an inert slot with a scripted memory budget, and asserts that parked KV segment backing is released before the headroom gate refuses, without evicting the resident slot. The test touches no disk, network or key material. It relates to T-041 (KV/prefix cache memory residency, A-001) only indirectly. It reinforces the intended posture that retained KV backing is freed under memory pressure, and does not weaken any control. The production behavior it exercises (ensureMemoryHeadroomForLoad releasing retained segments) is outside the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify it here. (2) LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift head lines 181-207 add forwardsServingStallRollbacksToProviderJob. It asserts that three rollback env keys (idle cache sweep, segment retention, segment host zeros) are in LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys and not in WatchdogAgent.passthroughEnvKeys. It also asserts that unrelated env vars (UNRELATED_SECRET) are excluded from the plist, so the allowlist pattern limits environment leakage into the launchd plist. This is consistent with T-043 (watchdog) and the TB-003 operator boundary. Passthrough of operator-set env is an existing mechanism. The actual allowlist and key definitions live in unchanged production code that was not supplied, so the real contents of these constants are unverified. Integration questions for the next pass: whether the production-side changes behind these tests (segment retention and host-zeros handling, idle cache sweep) clear or retain KV data in host memory consistently with T-028, and whether segmentHostZeros affects residual-data scrubbing. These are not visible in this batch. No regressions identified.
